join_note: Rows are matched to data/citation-register.json by URL, not by ID. The citation register and the audit register number their documents differently, so an ID join put one document's evidence beside another document's row. The IDs below are the citation register's.
purpose: Answer one question for a reader: is each cited document still retrievable, does the quote still appear, and did anything on the live listings contradict what this site publishes? A row records what the fetch showed, not what an earlier session recorded.
method: Each URL was fetched fresh, with no Associates sign-in and no session carried between fetches.
Quotations were compared against the fetched text, not against memory.

Prices, star ratings, review counts and customer review text were visible on the listing pages and were deliberately not recorded: citation-register constraints C1 and C2 allow them only through Amazon-served data or an API.

sources.what_the_fetch_showed: Section 1 requires links to use the special tagged link formats Amazon provides. Section 5 requires the Associates disclosure statement on the site.

Participation Requirements 2(b): the Associates ID or tag must appear as a URL parameter on each link placed on the site to an Amazon site. 2(b), 2(t) and 2(y) restrict prices, reviews and ratings, and price alerting. 2(w) prohibits shortening that obscures an Amazon destination. The IP License carries the Agent Terms.
Redirects to an Amazon sign-in page. No rate-card content is readable without an Associates account.

The disclosure must be close to the recommendation and be clear and conspicuous. The words paid link next to an affiliate link are described as adequate; the words affiliate link or buy now alone are not. A review that includes some negatives is still an endorsement.

16 CFR Part 255 is current. Section 255.5 is titled Disclosure of material connections and requires disclosure of a connection between the endorser and the seller that materially affects the weight or credibility of the endorsement.
An ASIN is a 10-character alphanumeric code assigned to every product, and it appears after /dp/ in a product URL.

Title, brand Art3d, sold by Art3d® and shipped by Amazon, the five-item bullet, and an Amazon's Choice badge. The product description section lists four line items, which is the inconsistency the audit already records.
Attribute table: aluminium, black, 2.56″L × 12.2″W, 5 ounces, 1 count, under-cabinet mount, sold by YH Urban. Bullet says self-adhesive or drilled. Three colour variants appear.

Iron, black, 9.17″D × 21.31″W × 16.61″H, eight tiers, three tool-free layouts. The title says lightweight cookware up to 11 inches; bullet 4 says up to 12 inches. A newer-model banner names B0BYYTQMTR.

listing_checks: Prices, star ratings, review counts and customer review text were visible on all three listing pages and none was recorded here or anywhere else in the repository.
No Amazon-hosted image was copied or hotlinked. The photography on this site is generated editorial imagery.
No claim in this file rests on a page that could not be fetched. S03 is the single exception and is marked unreachable rather than summarised.
questions_for_the_owner: Is the tracking ID shopnow047c-20 active for this site in the Associates account? Nothing outside the account can answer that, which is why no page claims a commission.
Which product did each submitted short link intend to point at? The observed destinations are recorded; the intention is not, and the intended fields stay blank until it is.

Should the three reference links keep an untagged listing URL, or be printed as plain ASINs until a validated Special Link exists? Both are published positions; F12 records the tension rather than hiding it.
